text: The stranger stood by the lamp and counted. Gus could see the hood move. One. Two. Three.
The hood turned. Not toward the noise. Toward Gus. As if the stranger had known all along exactly where he was.
Then a splash, a ring of green light on the water, and nothing.
Rollo, ashamed, ran to the waterline to make up for it. He came back dragging something on a chain.
A silver locket. Inside, a tiny painted face Gus had only ever seen in his mother’s photographs.
